defs.def: to give a lot of your time and effort to a particular activity or purpose because you think it is important 把 … 奉献给

ex.s: But in a larger sense, we can not dedicate — we can not consecrate — we can not hallow this ground.
ex.t: 但从更广义上说，我们不能奉献——我们不能圣化——我们不能神化这片土地。

ex.s: It is for us, the living, rather to be dedicated here to the unfinished work which they have, thus far, so nobly carried on.
ex.t: 倒是应该由我们，在世者，在此致力于他们至今高尚地推进的未竟事业。

defs.def: to say at the beginning of a book, a piece of music or a performance that you are doing it for sb, as a way of thanking them or showing respect （在书、音乐或演出的前部）题献辞

ex.s: Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth, upon this continent, a new nation, conceived in Liberty, and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.
ex.t: 四分七年前，我们的父亲在这个大陆上诞生了一个新的国家，这个国家是在自由中构想的，并致力于实现人人生而平等的主张。

defs.def: to hold an official ceremony to say that a building or an object has a special purpose or is special to the memory of a particular person 为 … 举行奉献典礼；为（建筑物等）举行落成典礼

ex.s: Now we are engaged in a great civil war, testing whether that nation, or any nation, so conceived, and so dedicated, can long endure.
ex.t: 现在我们正从事一场伟大的内战，以考验这个国家，或者任何一个孕育于自由并奉行上述原则的国家是否能够长久存在下去。

ex.s: We have come to dedicate a portion of it as a final resting place for those who here gave their lives that that nation might live.
ex.t: 我们来到这里，是要把这地方的一部分奉献为那些在此献身、让国家得以存续的人们的安息之所。
